Let $N\ge4$, $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$ be given by the coherent value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], and suppose some distinct $a,b$ satisfy $f(a)=f(b)$. For any $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the lazy Johnson walk has absolute gap $\delta=N/[2r(N-r)]$, marked stationary mass at least $\varepsilon=r(r-1)/[N(N-1)]$, stored-vertex setup value-query cost $r$, elementary replacement-update cost $2$, and check cost $0$. The controlled row-access construction of [[lem-qa-18-johnson-stored-data-query-access]] supplies stationary edge-state setup at most $r+2$, controlled row reflection at most $4$, and controlled two-reflection walk/inverse at most $8$ value queries. The reversible-walk finding theorem therefore gives a constant-success marked-subset finder with

$$r+O\!\left(\frac{N}{\sqrt r}\right)$$

value queries. Taking $r=\min\{\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\max\{2,\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor\}\}$ gives $O(N^{2/3})$ queries. A measured marked subset contains a colliding pair among its stored values, which can be output without further value queries; comparison gates are separate resources.

Let $N\ge2$, let $\mathcal V$ be a finite nonempty value set, and let $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$, where $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$. A **coherent value oracle** is a supplied finite unitary $O_f$ with an explicitly specified injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}:\mathcal V\to\{0,1\}^b$ for some finite $b$, and action $|i,z\rangle\mapsto|i,z\mathbin\oplus\operatorname{enc}(f(i))\rangle$ on valid addresses and target strings, as in [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]]. Injectivity ensures that stored encodings compare equal exactly when the underlying values do. Oracle-query cost and ordinary gate-occurrence cost are separate coordinates under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. The function table or name alone supplies no oracle circuit.

For $N\ge4$ and $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the **lazy Johnson walk** has state space $\Omega_r=\{S\subseteq[N]:|S|=r\}$ and transitions

$$P(S,S)=\tfrac12,\qquad P(S,S\setminus\{i\}\cup\{j\})=\frac{1}{2r(N-r)}\quad(i\in S,\ j\notin S),$$

with all other entries zero. Its marked vertices are

$$\mathcal M_f:=\{S\in\Omega_r:\exists i,j\in S,\ i\ne j,\ f(i)=f(j)\}.$$

The stored data at $S$ are the $r$ labeled values $(f(i))_{i\in S}$. Preparing the uniform $r$-subset state and loading these values has value-query cost $S_0=r$, with subset preparation gates charged separately. A neighbor update erases the removed value and loads the added value, so its value-query cost is $U_0=2$; the XOR oracle is its own inverse. Checking whether the stored subset is marked uses no further value queries, so $C_0=0$, but comparison gates and memory accesses are charged. After measuring a marked subset, scanning its stored values outputs a colliding pair with no additional value query; the scan's gate/time cost remains separate. For $N\le3$, use direct pairwise comparison rather than the $r$-subset walk. The lower bound $r\ge2$ is essential: a one-element subset cannot contain a collision pair.

Let a QRAM contain an ordered classical memory word $z=(z_0,\ldots,z_{L-1})\in\{0,1\}^L$, with $L\ge1$. Its **random-access quantum-memory gate** acts on an address register encoding $i\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, a target bit $b$, and the memory register by

$$|i,b,z_0\cdots z_{L-1}\rangle\longmapsto |i,z_i,z_0\cdots z_{i-1}b z_{i+1}\cdots z_{L-1}\rangle.$$

For address superpositions, this basis action is extended linearly. On valid addresses it swaps the target with the addressed memory bit, so the gate is an involutive permutation of the ordered computational basis and hence unitary; unused address encodings, if any, are fixed. One call has cost one QRAM gate-time unit by this model's convention. A read into a clean scratch target followed by copying and restoring the addressed bit uses the corresponding additional calls. The memory word itself, its address width, the circuit used to construct or update it, and the other ordinary gates are separate charged resources. This is a quantum random-access memory model; it does not assert an implementation by a bounded-arity ordinary circuit of the same gate count.

Let $n,m\ge0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be a total Boolean function on ordered bit strings. Its coherent XOR oracle is the linear extension of
$$
O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. The declared access contract states how many invocations count as queries and whether a controlled invocation is supplied. A query to this declared black box is counted separately from elementary gate size, depth, and width.

If $f$ is supplied instead by an explicit Boolean circuit, implementing $O_f$ means compiling that circuit and paying its reversible elementary-gate and workspace costs; the function description alone is not a free query. For this XOR oracle, its inverse is the same map, as proved in [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Controlled access remains a separate capability unless the contract explicitly provides it.

Inputs are integers $n,m\ge0$, $n$ distinct ordered Boolean input wires, an $m$-bit target register $y$ disjoint from the input wires, and a finite Boolean DAG with an explicit topological order and an ordered list of exactly $m$ output ports. Every vertex has a unique identifier; each non-input node is a constant $0$ or $1$, a NOT node of fan-in one, or an AND or OR node of fan-in two. Each source reference must name an input vertex or an earlier node in the supplied order. Each output port may name any input or non-input node, and repeated output ports are allowed. The Boolean graph uses the NOT/AND/OR basis with constants from [[def-boolean-circuit-size-depth-fanin-and-basis]], extended here to multiple ordered output ports sharing one graph.

Return INVALID if the input wires or graph vertices do not have distinct identifiers, a target wire overlaps an input or graph vertex, an unsupported gate or incorrect fan-in occurs, a source reference is unavailable at that position, the supplied order is invalid, or an output port names no available vertex. Otherwise:

1. Allocate one fresh clean value bit $w_v$ for each non-input node $v$.
2. Process nodes in the supplied order. Leave a constant-$0$ bit untouched; apply $X$ to a constant-$1$ bit. For a NOT node with input wire $u$, apply $X(w_v)$ then $\operatorname{CNOT}_{u\to w_v}$. For an AND node with inputs $u,v$, apply $T(u,v,w_v)$. For an OR node, apply $\operatorname{CNOT}_{u\to w_v}$, then $\operatorname{CNOT}_{v\to w_v}$, then $T(u,v,w_v)$. If a two-port node uses the same source identifier twice, first allocate a fresh clean scratch bit $s$, copy the source into $s$ by CNOT, use the distinct physical wires as the gate inputs, and uncopy $s$ immediately after writing $w_v$.
3. For each output port $j$, apply CNOT from its named input or value wire to target bit $y_j$.
4. Append the inverse of the entire node-evaluation list in reverse chronological order, including the temporary source-copy and uncopy instructions. Return the resulting finite gate list, with the input register unchanged and the target changed only by the stated XOR into $y$.

The inverse-list operation is defined instruction by instruction: $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli are each replaced by themselves, in reverse order. The Boolean graph is an explicit finite input; this procedure makes no uniform-generation, oracle, or Turing-time claim.

Let $n,m\ge0$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $y\in\{0,1\}^m$. Let a finite topologically ordered Boolean DAG have $S$ non-input nodes, including constants, and $E$ input-port uses counted with multiplicity. Its gates are NOT, AND, OR, and constants, with fan-in at most two, and it has $m$ ordered output ports computing $f(x)$. Under the fixed elementary alphabet in [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]], counting each occurrence of $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli as one gate and one serial layer, [[alg-qc-reversible-embedding]] returns a circuit on the ordered input, target, and work registers implementing
$$
|x,y,0^w\rangle\longmapsto|x,y\oplus f(x),0^w\rangle
$$
for every basis input $x$ and every target string $y$. It uses at most $6S+4E+m$ elementary gate occurrences, at most $S+E$ clean work bits, and serial depth at most $6S+4E+m$. The same operator action holds coherently on arbitrary superpositions and after adjoining any finite reference register.

For a finite Boolean DAG over constants, NOT, AND, and OR, with fan-in at most two, let $S$ be its number of non-input nodes, $E$ its number of input-port uses counted with multiplicity, and $m$ its number of ordered output ports. Let $D$ be the number of nonempty layers obtained by grouping each non-input node according to the maximum number of non-input vertices on a path ending at that node. Let $F$ be the maximum number of input-port occurrences from one source wire into gates in one such layer, with $F=0$ if there are no gate input ports. There is a layer-respecting reversible circuit implementing the same XOR embedding as [[alg-qc-reversible-embedding]] with $O(S+E+m)$ gate occurrences and $O(S+E+m)$ work bits. Let
$$
L=\lceil\log_2(F+1)\rceil,\qquad L_m=\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil.
$$
Its depth is at most
$$
2D(2L+3)+2L_m+1.
$$
The bound permits coherent fan-out of computational-basis labels by CNOT trees and does not assert arbitrary-state cloning or constant-factor preservation of Boolean-DAG depth. For bounded fan-in, $E\le2S$.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].
For every prime $p$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a field with exactly $p^n$ elements.
For every finite field $\mathbb F_q$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a monic irreducible polynomial in $\mathbb F_q[t]$ of degree $n$.

All bits are in $\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}$, with addition denoted by $\oplus$ and multiplication by juxtaposition. On three distinct ordered computational-basis wires, define the Toffoli gate $T$ and Fredkin gate $F$ by
$$
T|a,b,t\rangle=|a,b,t\oplus ab\rangle,
$$
and
$$
F|0,a,b\rangle=|0,a,b\rangle,\qquad F|1,a,b\rangle=|1,b,a\rangle.
$$
These basis actions extend linearly. Wire order is exactly the order displayed; the first two wires of $T$ are controls and the third is its target, while the first wire of $F$ is its control and the other two are conditionally swapped. Negative-control variants mean conjugating the chosen positive control by $X$ before and after the gate. These are fixed arity-three labels in the declared finite gate alphabet, not implicit access to arbitrary multicontrol gates. Their reversibility is established in [[lem-qc-x-cnot-toffoli-and-fredkin-are-involutions]].

Let $(X,P,\pi)$ be a finite ergodic reversible chain with actual absolute spectral gap $\delta_{\rm act}\in(0,1]$. Supply the algorithm with a dyadic rational lower bound $\delta_0\in(0,\delta_{\rm act}]$ and suppose the marked set is empty or has stationary mass at least the dyadic rational lower bound $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$. Let the dyadic rational failure target be $\rho\in(0,1)$. Let $S_0$ be the cost of preparing the stationary walk state, $U_0$ a common upper bound for one controlled $W$ or $W^*$ update and the exact controlled row-space reflection $R_A$ used by the construction, and $C$ the cost of a coherent marked check. For $0<\varepsilon_0<1/2$, one outer trial of [[alg-qa-18-reversible-walk-finding]] with gap input $\delta_0$ has one-sided error, finds a marked state with a fixed positive probability when one exists, and uses

$$S_0+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0}}\left(\frac{U_0}{\sqrt{\delta_0}}+C\right)\right).$$

in the corresponding query/update/check cost coordinates. The capped wrapper with failure target $\rho\in(0,1)$ uses $O((S_0+\varepsilon_0^{-1/2}(U_0/\sqrt{\delta_0}+C))(1+\ln(1/\rho)))$ in that profile. When $\varepsilon_0\ge1/2$, its direct-sampling branch uses $O((S_0+C)(1+\ln(1/\rho)))$. If the actual gap is dyadic and supplied exactly, one may set $\delta_0=\delta_{\rm act}$; otherwise a dyadic lower bound within a factor of two gives the same asymptotic bound in the actual gap. For gate, width, precision, and bit-time coordinates, the phase-register gates, controlled reflection, comparisons, numerical generation, and retained workspace are charged separately.

Let $N\ge4096$, $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, and $f:[N]\to[M]$ with the injective value encoding in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]]. Put $H=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$, $d=C=16\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil$, $R=2^{\lceil\log_2r\rceil}$, and $q=2^H$, and assume $d\le N$. Fix as part of the representation a monic irreducible polynomial of degree $H$ over $\mathbb F_2$ and its polynomial-basis field $\mathbb F_q$; the storage is canonical relative to this fixed field representation and the hash seed. Choose $H+1$ independent uniform coefficient tuples in $\mathbb F_q^d$ and use them as coefficients of degree-at-most-$(d-1)$ polynomials $p_{-1},p_0,\ldots,p_{H-1}$. For each $i\in[N]$, let $\mathsf{enc}(i)$ be the field element whose $H$-bit polynomial-basis coordinate string is the $H$-bit binary encoding of $i-1$; these elements are distinct. Let $h(i)$ be the integer represented by the low $\log_2R$ bits of $p_{-1}(\mathsf{enc}(i))$, and let $b_\ell(i)$ be the low bit of $p_\ell(\mathsf{enc}(i))$. The **height** of $i$ is the number of consecutive $1$ bits starting at $b_0(i)$, capped at $H$; equivalently, $\operatorname{height}(i)\ge\ell$ exactly when $b_0(i)=\cdots=b_{\ell-1}(i)=1$.

For a subset $S\in\binom{[N]}r$, the fixed memory word has $R$ hash buckets, each with $C$ slots, and one overflow bit. If no bucket exceeds capacity, every $i\in S$ is stored in bucket $h(i)$; occupied slots are sorted by index, and each record contains $i$, $f(i)$, and its skip-list fields. A node identifier is the input index $i$; resolving it means computing $h(i)$ and scanning that bucket. If any bucket would exceed capacity, set the overflow bit and put the same fixed sentinel in the data slots. Thus the represented word is a total, unique function of the subset and seed; the skip-list structure is valid exactly when the overflow bit is zero.

The storage also contains two **nested skip lists**, one in increasing index order and one in lexicographic order of $(f(i),i)$. Level $\ell$ of either list, for $0\le\ell\le H$, contains exactly the keys with height at least $\ell$; level $0$ contains all keys. Each forward pointer names a node identifier and stores its **span**, the difference between the source and target ranks in level $0$ (the head sentinel has rank $-1$). These spans support rank and select operations. The two lists, bucket positions, pointers, and spans are the unique ones determined by $(S,f|_S,p_{-1},p_0,\ldots,p_{H-1})$; they do not depend on the path used to reach $S$. A capped search inspects at most $D=2\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1$ forward entries at each level before raising an overrun flag. This definition specifies a finite representation and search convention; it does not assert a probability or cost bound.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

Let $m\ge1$ and $Q=2^m$. Count costs in the ideal continuous-rotation submodel, where each exact controlled phase used by the binary QFT is one gate. If the controlled powers $C(U^{2^j})$, $0\le j<m$, are supplied as one query each, one run uses exactly $m$ controlled-power queries. If the only oracle is $C(U)$, the repeated implementation uses exactly $Q-1$ controlled-$U$ queries. If the supplied controlled-power circuits have ordinary gate counts $C_j$, the unitary gate count after the eigenstate input is provided is
$$\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}C_j+2m+\frac{m(m-1)}2+\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor.$$
The final register measurement reads $m$ bits and is not included in this unitary gate count. No cost-free power construction, fixed finite gate alphabet, uniform family, or state-preparation bound is asserted.

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

Let $V$ be a normed space. For all $x,y\in V$,
$$\bigl|\|x\|-\|y\|\bigr|\le \|x-y\|.$$
In particular, the norm map is $1$-Lipschitz for the norm metric.

Let $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite instrument from a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$ to a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $K$, with finite nonempty observed outcome set $\Omega$. After observing $a$, suppose the circuit applies a specified finite unitary suffix $S_a$ on $K$. For every finite-dimensional complex inner-product reference space $R$ and every input operator $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$, the measured circuit's unnormalized branch on $K\otimes R$ is
$$\mathcal J_a^{(R)}(X):=(S_a\otimes I_R)(\mathcal I_a^{(R)}(X))(S_a^\dagger\otimes I_R),$$
where, after choosing an ordered orthonormal basis of $R$, $\mathcal I_a^{(R)}$ denotes the finite ancillary block amplification on $\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$: if $X=[X_{kl}]$, then $\mathcal I_a^{(R)}(X)=[\mathcal I_a(X_{kl})]$. This is the block extension in the complete-positivity definition. The coherent construction retains the observed label register until terminal readout. Its outcome-$a$ branch, after tracing out the hidden Kraus and padding registers but retaining the label, is $\mathcal J_a^{(R)}(X)\otimes|e_a\rangle\langle e_a|$ on $K\otimes R$ and the label register (up to the canonical factor permutation); discarding the label gives the same data-reference branch map. Thus it preserves the complete outcome law and all correlations with $R$. This is an exact denotational statement: any newly used dilation or block operation must be listed and charged by a gate or oracle model; no same-alphabet synthesis or cost bound is asserted.

derivations.claim: For $N\ge4096$, the clamp in [F1] is $r=\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor$. Set $m=\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil$, $H=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$, $d=C=16m$, $R=2^{\lceil\log_2r\rceil}$, and $q=2^H$. The function $(\log_2(x+2)+1)/x^{2/3}$ decreases for $x\ge4096$, because its logarithmic derivative is $1/((x+2)\ln2(\log_2(x+2)+1))-2/(3x)<0$; indeed $2(x+2)\ln2(\log_2(x+2)+1)>3x$ there. Since $\log_2(4098)<13$, this gives $d\le16(\log_2(N+2)+1)\le224N^{2/3}/256=7N^{2/3}/8$. Also $r\ge N^{2/3}-1\ge255N^{2/3}/256$, so $d\le r\le N/2$ and $d\le N\le q$. Finally $r\le R<2r\le N$. By [F9], fix a polynomial-basis representation of $\mathbb F_q$; its irreducible polynomial is a finite hardwired setup description whose generation time is separate.

For fixed $S$ and seed, place each $(i,f(i))$ in its hash bucket and build the two canonical lists of [F12]. Pad each list to a power-of-two length $L=O(r)$ with sentinels. A bitonic sorting network recursively sorts the two halves in opposite directions and merges them by comparing pairs at distance $L/2$, then recursively merging both halves. A bitonic sequence becomes, after thresholding its keys at any fixed threshold, a circular interval of $1$ bits; the half-distance compare-exchanges place either all $0$ bits in the low half or all $1$ bits in the high half, leaving each half bitonic. Let $n,m\ge0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be a total Boolean function on ordered bit strings. Its coherent XOR oracle is the linear extension of
$$
O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. The declared access contract states how many invocations count as queries and whether a controlled invocation is supplied. A query to this declared black box is counted separately from elementary gate size, depth, and width.

If $f$ is supplied instead by an explicit Boolean circuit, implementing $O_f$ means compiling that circuit and paying its reversible elementary-gate and workspace costs; the function description alone is not a free query. For this XOR oracle, its inverse is the same map, as proved in [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Controlled access remains a separate capability unless the contract explicitly provides it.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

Let a QRAM contain an ordered classical memory word $z=(z_0,\ldots,z_{L-1})\in\{0,1\}^L$, with $L\ge1$. Its **random-access quantum-memory gate** acts on an address register encoding $i\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, a target bit $b$, and the memory register by

$$|i,b,z_0\cdots z_{L-1}\rangle\longmapsto |i,z_i,z_0\cdots z_{i-1}b z_{i+1}\cdots z_{L-1}\rangle.$$

For address superpositions, this basis action is extended linearly. On valid addresses it swaps the target with the addressed memory bit, so the gate is an involutive permutation of the ordered computational basis and hence unitary; unused address encodings, if any, are fixed. One call has cost one QRAM gate-time unit by this model's convention. A read into a clean scratch target followed by copying and restoring the addressed bit uses the corresponding additional calls. The memory word itself, its address width, the circuit used to construct or update it, and the other ordinary gates are separate charged resources. This is a quantum random-access memory model; it does not assert an implementation by a bounded-arity ordinary circuit of the same gate count.

derivations.claim: The parity oracle is exactly one application of the supplied $O_{f_m}$, so its query count is one by [F1]. In an ordinary circuit, form the interaction graph whose vertices are all circuit wires and whose edges join the two wires acted on by each two-wire gate occurrence. If the target's connected component omitted an address bit, then no gate couples that bit to the target or to any intermediary on its component; the circuit factors across this separation, making the target output independent of the omitted bit. This contradicts parity's dependence on each input bit: fixing the other bits and changing the omitted bit changes the target. Hence the graph contains a connected subgraph joining the target and all $m$ address wires. Any connected graph containing these $m+1$ distinct terminals has at least $m$ edges, even if it also contains ancilla vertices; each edge comes from a gate occurrence.

For the explicit upper-bound constructions, choose an ordinary gate alphabet containing CNOT, with basis action $|a,b\rangle\mapsto|a,b\oplus a\rangle$; this is an additional model choice, not a consequence of [F2]. Applying the $m$ CNOT gates from each address bit to the target computes parity into that target and gives an exact $m$-gate implementation. In QRAM, store $z_i=f_m(i)$ and use one addressed swap to move $z_i$ to a clean scratch bit, copy it by CNOT into the oracle target, and use a second addressed swap to restore the memory and clear the scratch. This is a constant number of RAM calls by [F3], but it still requires the table to have been constructed and maintained. The online gate models therefore count one oracle call versus at least $m$ ordinary two-wire gates for this function, with RAM construction cost recorded separately.

Let $N\ge4$ and $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. For the lazy Johnson transition matrix $P$ on the $r$-subsets of $[N]$ from [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], all eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are

$$\lambda_j=1-\frac{j(N+1-j)}{2r(N-r)},\qquad 0\le j\le r,$$

with multiplicity $\binom Nj-\binom N{j-1}$, where $\binom N{-1}=0$. They are nonnegative, and for the uniform stationary law the absolute spectral gap, in the sense of [[def-qa-17-absolute-spectral-gap]], is

$$\delta(P)=1-\lambda_1=\frac{N}{2r(N-r)}.$$

Let $N\ge4$, $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$ be given by the coherent value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], and suppose some distinct $a,b$ satisfy $f(a)=f(b)$. For any $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the lazy Johnson walk has absolute gap $\delta=N/[2r(N-r)]$, marked stationary mass at least $\varepsilon=r(r-1)/[N(N-1)]$, stored-vertex setup value-query cost $r$, elementary replacement-update cost $2$, and check cost $0$. The controlled row-access construction of [[lem-qa-18-johnson-stored-data-query-access]] supplies stationary edge-state setup at most $r+2$, controlled row reflection at most $4$, and controlled two-reflection walk/inverse at most $8$ value queries. The reversible-walk finding theorem therefore gives a constant-success marked-subset finder with

$$r+O\!\left(\frac{N}{\sqrt r}\right)$$

value queries. Taking $r=\min\{\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\max\{2,\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor\}\}$ gives $O(N^{2/3})$ queries. A measured marked subset contains a colliding pair among its stored values, which can be output without further value queries; comparison gates are separate resources.

Let $N\ge2$, let $\mathcal V$ be a finite nonempty value set, and let $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$, where $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$. A **coherent value oracle** is a supplied finite unitary $O_f$ with an explicitly specified injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}:\mathcal V\to\{0,1\}^b$ for some finite $b$, and action $|i,z\rangle\mapsto|i,z\mathbin\oplus\operatorname{enc}(f(i))\rangle$ on valid addresses and target strings, as in [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]]. Injectivity ensures that stored encodings compare equal exactly when the underlying values do. Oracle-query cost and ordinary gate-occurrence cost are separate coordinates under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. The function table or name alone supplies no oracle circuit.

For $N\ge4$ and $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the **lazy Johnson walk** has state space $\Omega_r=\{S\subseteq[N]:|S|=r\}$ and transitions

$$P(S,S)=\tfrac12,\qquad P(S,S\setminus\{i\}\cup\{j\})=\frac{1}{2r(N-r)}\quad(i\in S,\ j\notin S),$$

with all other entries zero. Its marked vertices are

$$\mathcal M_f:=\{S\in\Omega_r:\exists i,j\in S,\ i\ne j,\ f(i)=f(j)\}.$$

The stored data at $S$ are the $r$ labeled values $(f(i))_{i\in S}$. Preparing the uniform $r$-subset state and loading these values has value-query cost $S_0=r$, with subset preparation gates charged separately. A neighbor update erases the removed value and loads the added value, so its value-query cost is $U_0=2$; the XOR oracle is its own inverse. Checking whether the stored subset is marked uses no further value queries, so $C_0=0$, but comparison gates and memory accesses are charged. After measuring a marked subset, scanning its stored values outputs a colliding pair with no additional value query; the scan's gate/time cost remains separate. For $N\le3$, use direct pairwise comparison rather than the $r$-subset walk. The lower bound $r\ge2$ is essential: a one-element subset cannot contain a collision pair.

Their multiplicities are $1$, $\binom51-\binom50=4$, and $\binom52-\binom51=5$, totaling $10=\binom52$. Thus the nonconstant top eigenvalue is $7/12$ and the gap is $5/12$. An independent finite check enumerates the ten $2$-subsets lexicographically and forms the integer matrix $B_{ST}=12P(S,T)$: its diagonal is $6$, and its off-diagonal entry is $1$ exactly when $|S\cap T|=1$. Exact determinant expansion gives $\det(xI-B)=(x-12)(x-7)^4(x-4)^5$, confirming the scaled spectrum. A fixed colliding pair lies in $\binom30=1$ of the $10$ subsets, so its marked fraction is $1/10$.

For $N=6,r=3$, the denominator is $18$. Formula [F1] gives eigenvalues $1,2/3,4/9,1/3$ for $j=0,1,2,3$. Their multiplicities are $1,5,9,5$, totaling $20=\binom63$. The gap is $1-2/3=1/3$. A fixed pair belongs to $\binom41=4$ of the $20$ subsets, hence has marked fraction $1/5$.

Under the stated assumption that the only collision pairs are the two named disjoint pairs, each pair is contained in four $3$-subsets, and no $3$-subset contains both pairs because their union has four elements. The two marked families are therefore disjoint and their union has $4+4=8$ subsets, a fraction $8/20=2/5$. The value exceeds the one-pair lower bound $1/5$, as required by the “at least” in [F2]. Without the exclusivity assumptions, the counted families still give lower bounds for the marked fraction, but extra collisions can increase it.

Let $N\ge2$, let $\mathcal V$ be a finite nonempty value set, and let $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$, where $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$. A **coherent value oracle** is a supplied finite unitary $O_f$ with an explicitly specified injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}:\mathcal V\to\{0,1\}^b$ for some finite $b$, and action $|i,z\rangle\mapsto|i,z\mathbin\oplus\operatorname{enc}(f(i))\rangle$ on valid addresses and target strings, as in [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]]. Injectivity ensures that stored encodings compare equal exactly when the underlying values do. Oracle-query cost and ordinary gate-occurrence cost are separate coordinates under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. The function table or name alone supplies no oracle circuit.

For $N\ge4$ and $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the **lazy Johnson walk** has state space $\Omega_r=\{S\subseteq[N]:|S|=r\}$ and transitions

$$P(S,S)=\tfrac12,\qquad P(S,S\setminus\{i\}\cup\{j\})=\frac{1}{2r(N-r)}\quad(i\in S,\ j\notin S),$$

with all other entries zero. Its marked vertices are

$$\mathcal M_f:=\{S\in\Omega_r:\exists i,j\in S,\ i\ne j,\ f(i)=f(j)\}.$$

The stored data at $S$ are the $r$ labeled values $(f(i))_{i\in S}$. Preparing the uniform $r$-subset state and loading these values has value-query cost $S_0=r$, with subset preparation gates charged separately. A neighbor update erases the removed value and loads the added value, so its value-query cost is $U_0=2$; the XOR oracle is its own inverse. Checking whether the stored subset is marked uses no further value queries, so $C_0=0$, but comparison gates and memory accesses are charged. After measuring a marked subset, scanning its stored values outputs a colliding pair with no additional value query; the scan's gate/time cost remains separate. For $N\le3$, use direct pairwise comparison rather than the $r$-subset walk. The lower bound $r\ge2$ is essential: a one-element subset cannot contain a collision pair.

Let $N\ge4$, $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$ be given by the coherent value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], and suppose some distinct $a,b$ satisfy $f(a)=f(b)$. For any $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the lazy Johnson walk has absolute gap $\delta=N/[2r(N-r)]$, marked stationary mass at least $\varepsilon=r(r-1)/[N(N-1)]$, stored-vertex setup value-query cost $r$, elementary replacement-update cost $2$, and check cost $0$. The controlled row-access construction of [[lem-qa-18-johnson-stored-data-query-access]] supplies stationary edge-state setup at most $r+2$, controlled row reflection at most $4$, and controlled two-reflection walk/inverse at most $8$ value queries. The reversible-walk finding theorem therefore gives a constant-success marked-subset finder with

$$r+O\!\left(\frac{N}{\sqrt r}\right)$$

value queries. Taking $r=\min\{\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\max\{2,\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor\}\}$ gives $O(N^{2/3})$ queries. A measured marked subset contains a colliding pair among its stored values, which can be output without further value queries; comparison gates are separate resources.

derivations.claim: For $N=8,r=4$, the state space has $\binom84=70$ subsets. Exactly $\binom62=15$ contain the unique colliding pair, so $\varepsilon=15/70=3/14$, equal to $r(r-1)/[N(N-1)]=12/56$. The stationary mass is positive, and [F1] gives four setup value queries, two value queries per update, and no extra value query for the stored-value check.

More generally, for $r=\Theta(N^{2/3})$ with $r\le N/2$, [F2] gives setup $r=\Theta(N^{2/3})$ and update/search term $N/\sqrt r=\Theta(N^{2/3})$. Thus both terms are of the same asymptotic order and the theorem's total is $O(N^{2/3})$. For $N=8$, the clamp in the theorem selects $r=4$; its expression is $4+O(8/2)=4+O(4)$, consistent with this scaling.

Let $n,m\ge0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be a total Boolean function on ordered bit strings. Its coherent XOR oracle is the linear extension of
$$
O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. The declared access contract states how many invocations count as queries and whether a controlled invocation is supplied. A query to this declared black box is counted separately from elementary gate size, depth, and width.

If $f$ is supplied instead by an explicit Boolean circuit, implementing $O_f$ means compiling that circuit and paying its reversible elementary-gate and workspace costs; the function description alone is not a free query. For this XOR oracle, its inverse is the same map, as proved in [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Controlled access remains a separate capability unless the contract explicitly provides it.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

For a finite-dimensional unitary $U$, **inverse access** is the explicitly granted operation $U^\dagger=U^{-1}$. Its availability and query or gate charge are recorded separately from forward access, including any controlled access in [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]]. For a chronological sequence of length $k\ge0$ that applies $U_1$ first and $U_k$ last, the total operator is $W=U_k\cdots U_1$ when $k>0$ and $W=I_H$ when $k=0$. For $k>0$, the inverse sequence applies $U_k^\dagger$ first, then $U_{k-1}^\dagger$, down to $U_1^\dagger$; for $k=0$ it is the empty sequence.

For a nonempty finite row-stochastic kernel $(X,P)$, a **row-preparation access model** supplies an explicit bijection $\eta:X\to\{0,\ldots,|X|-1\}$; write $\kappa_x$ for the image of $x$ under this bijection. Every ket $|x\rangle$ below denotes the basis vector $|\kappa_x\rangle$. The model supplies a finite work register $W$ with a specified clean unit vector $|0_W\rangle$ and a unitary $V_P$ on the ordered register product $\mathbb C^X\otimes\mathbb C^X\otimes W$ satisfying

$$V_P\bigl(|x\rangle\otimes|0\rangle\otimes|0_W\rangle\bigr)=\left(|x\rangle\otimes\sum_y\sqrt{P_{xy}}|y\rangle\right)\otimes|0_W\rangle\qquad(x\in X).$$

The state encoding and its description are part of the supplied circuit interface and are included in the circuit description or uniform generator. The model separately declares access and costs for the forward call $V_P$, inverse call $V_P^*$, controlled $V_P$, controlled $V_P^*$, a direct range-reflection call, controlled range-reflection access, the clean-state reflection $R_0$, controlled $R_0$, the swap on the first two registers, and controlled swap access. The clean-state reflection is

$$R_0:=2\bigl(I_X\otimes|0,0_W\rangle\langle0,0_W|\bigr)-I,$$

where the second register and work register are in their specified clean states. When range reflection is implemented from row preparation, the supplied circuit word is $V_PR_0V_P^*$; the access-cost theorem proves that on the clean-work subspace it realizes the logical reflection $2TT^*-I$. The swap acts as $S$ on the first two registers and as the identity on $W$.

Query calls, gate counts, circuit-description bits, uniform-generation time, and precision are separate cost coordinates. A controlled walk implemented factor by factor needs controlled access to each constituent, including the preparation calls, $R_0$, and the swap. A matrix $P$ by itself supplies none of these circuits or efficient costs. For a family of encoded chains, a uniform circuit family is an additional explicit input, not a consequence of the finite matrix definition.

For a nonempty chain in the row-preparation implementation of [[def-qa-17-walk-access-model]], the full-workspace word $S V_P R_0 V_P^*$ restricts on the clean-work subspace to the logical one-reflection step $U=S(2TT^*-I)$. One such uncontrolled step uses exactly one call each to $V_P^*$ and $V_P$, one clean-state reflection $R_0$, and one swap $S$. The factorwise controlled implementation controls each constituent, including both row-preparation calls, $R_0$, and $S$; this count describes that implementation. A $W=U^2$ step uses exactly two such $U$ implementations. Query calls, gate counts, description bits, uniform-generation time, and precision are recorded as separate cost coordinates.

Let $(v_0,\ldots,v_{r-1})$ be a finite linearly independent list in a real or complex inner product space. There is an orthonormal list $(e_0,\ldots,e_{r-1})$ such that, for every $k\le r$,

$$\operatorname{span}(e_0,\ldots,e_{k-1})=\operatorname{span}(v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}).$$

It is obtained recursively from

$$u_k=v_k-\sum_{j<k}\langle v_k,e_j\rangle e_j,\qquad e_k=\frac{u_k}{\lVert u_k\rVert}.$$

For $r=0$, both lists are empty.

derivations.claim: Encode a vertex by the computational basis vector $|S,d_f(S)\rangle$. Distinct subsets have orthogonal encodings, so replacing each logical vertex basis vector by this encoding is an isometry, as is its two-register tensor square. Subset arithmetic, label permutations, copying computational-basis data by XOR, and finite unitaries depending only on $N,r$ issue no value queries. A specified unit vector can be completed to an orthonormal basis as follows: append the computational basis in fixed order, retain each vector outside the preceding span, and apply [F5]. The resulting list spans and retains the initial unit vector; the linear map between the computational basis and this basis preserves squared coordinate norms and is invertible, hence unitary. In particular, prepare the uniform subset superposition with this exact finite unitary as its first column, then load the $r$ ordered values by $r$ queries. The claim is a query bound only: neither the number of gates of that unitary nor a uniform generator is being bounded.

From the encoded source vertex and a blank target register, a finite unitary depending only on $N,r$ prepares the second subset label in the Johnson row distribution: amplitude $1/\sqrt2$ for $T=S$ and $1/\sqrt{2r(N-r)}$ for every $T=S-\{i\}+\{j\}$. For each source label this is a unit vector, and different sources stay orthogonal because the source register is unchanged; use the finite completion from step 1.1 in each source-label block to define a unitary on the padded registers. Reversible label arithmetic identifies the unique new index $j$ on a non-loop branch, and uses the fixed valid address $1$ on the loop branch. Copy to the target all values whose indices lie in $S\cap T$, using the source stored values. Query $f(j)$ into clean scratch, XOR it into the target new-value slot only on a non-loop branch, and query again to erase scratch. For a loop, copy the entire stored list and leave the computed scratch unused before erasing it. Uncompute the address and index-arithmetic scratch from $S,T$. Thus two queries implement the encoded row isometry with all scratch clean. The row operation extends unitarily outside the valid-data subspace; no oracle-dependent table is hardwired into the nonquery gates.

Initialize the address scratch to the fixed valid address $1$. To control this circuit, control its nonquery gates, leaving that address at $1$ on the control-zero branch, and still compute $f(j)$ and erase it with the same two unconditional oracle calls; the middle XOR into the new-value slot is controlled by both the outer control and the non-loop flag. On control zero the two queries cancel and all other registers are fixed. Thus controlled row preparation costs two queries. Reverse the complete word for either inverse; it also costs two queries. Let the whole target-and-work register have a specified blank vector $|0_{\rm tgt}\rangle$. The query-free reflection $$I_{\rm src}\otimes\bigl(2|0_{\rm tgt}\rangle\langle0_{\rm tgt}|-I_{\rm tgt}\bigr)$$ acts on the entire source register, including invalid source encodings; it performs no test for membership in the function-dependent set of valid encodings. Conjugating it by the row-preparation unitary gives the reflection about the image of all blank-target source states. The row-preparation unitary preserves the source register, so images of invalid source basis encodings stay orthogonal to logical encoded walk states. On the logical encoded subspace, the conjugated reflection therefore restricts to the range reflection transported by the isometry in step 1.1. Possible invalid data encodings never enter a logical walk state.

By [F4], one row reflection costs four queries, since its middle blank-state phase is query-free. Swapping both vertex-and-data blocks is query-free and preserves the valid encoding. Hence one controlled $U$ costs four queries and controlled $W=U^2$ costs eight; their inverses have the same counts. Preparing the encoded uniform first vertex costs $r$, and one row call adds two, giving stationary edge-state setup at most $r+2$. Markedness depends only on the stored first-vertex values and requires no further value query. All control predicates, comparisons, state preparation gates and retained registers remain separate charged resources.
